description: Error fingerprint database mapping stack traces, error messages, and symptoms to root causes and quick resolutions.

patterns: No market data during competing live session
Trading TWS session is connected from a different IP address
fingerprints.symptom: Market data is frozen across all bots; tick stream stops; no trades execute; watchdog reports no bar data.
fingerprints.root_cause: Simultaneous live and paper IBKR sessions for the same user (e.g. ib-gateway-live running concurrently with ib-gateway-paper, or an active session on IBKR Mobile / Desktop TWS / Web Portal). IBKR enforces single-session market data rules for shared market data subscriptions.
fingerprints.resolution: Stop competing gateway/session (e.g. 'sudo docker stop ib-gateway-live' or log out of mobile/web TWS), then restart the trading bot manager ('sudo systemctl restart trading-bot-manager').

patterns: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes
fingerprints.symptom: Trade timestamps mismatched or offset datetime error in Firestore/calculations
fingerprints.root_cause: datetime.now() without tzinfo parameter used instead of UTC aware datetime.
fingerprints.resolution: Use datetime.now(timezone.utc) or utcnow() helper. All Firestore timestamps must be offset-aware UTC.

patterns: IBKR execution report for closed position
fingerprints.symptom: Bot triggers exit callback for position no longer held or duplicate trade record.
fingerprints.root_cause: _on_exec_details processed IBKR execution reports without verifying live position status or deduplicating execution IDs.
fingerprints.resolution: Check ib.positions() before processing fill and enforce exec_id deduplication set in log_trade().

fingerprints.symptom: Bot receives 0 historical bars on startup and remains inactive.
fingerprints.root_cause: Requesting bar_size '1 hour' at open before enough bars exist or using whatToShow='MIDPOINT' instead of 'TRADES'.

patterns: covered call pnl missing in tick exit
fingerprints.symptom: Tick-based exit calculations evaluate covered call P&L as 0.0.
fingerprints.root_cause: on_tick_update_entries did not pass resolved Bucket object to _check_exit_conditions.
fingerprints.resolution: Pass bucket parameter explicitly to _check_exit_conditions to pull bucket.option_pnl.

fingerprints.symptom: Bot classified as unhealthy on latency spike or thrashing exit attempts.
fingerprints.root_cause: Unhealthy threshold set too low (3 timeouts) or profit floor exit lacked cooldown.
fingerprints.resolution: Set unhealthy threshold to 7 timeouts and add 60-second cooldown on exit retries.

fingerprints.symptom: IBKR fills order after bot gave up waiting, causing untracked position.
fingerprints.root_cause: Timeout logic in execution_manager did not retain order_id for post-timeout fill callbacks. v4.5 also found enter_bucket registered the pending entry only AFTER place_order() returned, so an execDetails firing during the call was dropped; pending entries from the `result is None` path stored no order_id, so _handle_async_fill could never adopt them.
fingerprints.resolution: Use AsyncFillMonitor to track timed-out order IDs for 60 seconds (max_retries 6 x 10s). v4.5: register pending_entry_orders BEFORE place_order and guard against double-processing; _handle_async_fill falls back to side+quantity matching when no order_id is stored; verify_no_orphaned_position grants a 120s grace for fresh in-flight entries; exit-position refresh waits for the target symbol.

fingerprints.symptom: Realized P/L is duplicated/inflated in logs or IBKR position mismatch reported on startup after exit timeout.
fingerprints.root_cause: exit_handler checked 'if order_result:' which evaluates to True for (None, order_id) 2-tuples on timeout. Strategy on_exit_fill lacked 'if self.active_position is None: return' guard.
fingerprints.resolution: Check 'if order_result and order_result[0] is not None:' before setting success=True. Add active_position is None guard in on_exit_fill. Allow manual/orphaned exit orders with bucket_id=None.

fingerprints.symptom: Emergency or manual market exit orders stall in PendingSubmit and timeout during extended hours trading.
fingerprints.root_cause: US stock exchanges prohibit Market orders outside Regular Trading Hours (9:30 AM - 4:00 PM ET), causing IBKR to hold MarketOrders until market open.
fingerprints.resolution: Route all orders outside RTH to limit_escalation (LimitOrder with outsideRth=True).

fingerprints.symptom: Running --close-all via CLI keeps python process running in background, causing Client ID 3 socket conflict on next service start.
fingerprints.root_cause: run_trader in launcher.py invoked trader.run() after close_all_positions() instead of disconnecting and exiting immediately.
fingerprints.resolution: Update launcher.py to call trader.disconnect() and sys.exit(0) immediately after close_all_positions(). Add reqHistoricalData price fallback in base.py if ticker returns None or NaN.

fingerprints.symptom: IDE error or TypeError raised during _legacy_close_position invocation.
fingerprints.root_cause: _legacy_close_position passed limit_price and urgency kwargs to place_order which accepts price, is_exit, reason, bucket_id.
fingerprints.resolution: Pass price=price, is_exit=True, reason=reason, bucket_id=bucket.bucket_id to place_order and unpack tuple return value (fill_price, order_id).

fingerprints.symptom: After a churn exit the bot re-enters immediately; the suppression log shows a peak of $0.00 / direction LONG on every churn exit.
fingerprints.root_cause: on_exit_fill() assigned self.active_position = None BEFORE calling _arm_re_entry_suppression(), so (self.active_position or {}).get('peak_price') was always 0.0 and direction defaulted to LONG. The ~1 ATR breakout early-clear then fired on the first tick check (tick >= 0 + ATR), lifting the block instantly.
fingerprints.resolution: Snapshot exit_peak_price and exit_direction from active_position inside the lock before clearing, then pass them explicitly to _arm_re_entry_suppression(reason, exit_peak_price=..., exit_direction=...). Never read active_position after it is cleared.

fingerprints.symptom: Feedback engine logs '✏️ peak_giveback_min_r[REGIME]: X → Y (forked from global)' but adaptive_pnl.effective_thresholds stays {} and the global scalar never changes.
fingerprints.root_cause: Target bucket resolved with 'getattr(config, 'effective_thresholds', None) or {}'. An empty (falsy) effective_thresholds takes the 'or {}' branch, allocating a throwaway dict; setdefault() mutations are written to that temp dict, not the config — nudge silently lost.
fingerprints.resolution: Use an explicit None check instead of 'or {}': buckets = getattr(config, 'effective_thresholds', None); if buckets is None: buckets = {}. Reattach buckets to the config attrs so setdefault() mutates the live dict.

patterns: bot exits with code 1 immediately after start
fingerprints.symptom: A bot starts and exits with code 1 within seconds of every start. The supervisor restarts it every ~5s (dozens of times in minutes) and the operator sees only the debounced 'Trading Bot Down' email - the critical 'restart failure persisting' alert never fires.
fingerprints.root_cause: The bot's config cannot be constructed - typically a config write that bypassed a cross-section invariant (D18: max_hold_hours below the covered-call horizon floor) - so load_trading_config() raises at module level under __main__ and the process exits 1. Popen itself succeeded, so the supervisor counted a *successful start* and reset its failure counter; the persistent-failure branch was unreachable for the most common cause of a bot failing to trade. A deploy that failed the #222 config-code gate then restarted the fleet anyway, turning one broken config into a fleet-wide bounce.
fingerprints.resolution: Fix the write path so the persisted value satisfies the invariant the loader enforces (D18: bots #350). The supervisor now counts process deaths, not just Popen failures, and escalates after 3 consecutive deaths with a 120s backoff (bots #355). The deploy rollback restarts the services only when that run had already restarted them, so a gate failure leaves the running fleet untouched (bots #354).

patterns: Not all enabled bots are running after 12 attempts
Deploy to Trading VM (Daily) failure at Verify bots are running
fingerprints.symptom: The deploy fails at 'Verify bots are running' and rolls the code back. Off-hours (the bots are stopped by design) the gate cannot pass, so the nightly deploy - which fires at 03:00 UTC = 23:00 ET, inside the stopped window - always rolls back and never delivers the code.
fingerprints.root_cause: The verify gate asks `bot_manager.py --status-json`, which exits 0 iff EVERY enabled bot runs. The fleet only runs 08:51-16:39 ET (systemd timers) and `bot_manager.py::_is_market_active` refuses to run a bot outside 08:45-16:45 ET on a weekday, so outside that window 'the bots are not running' is the intended state - but the gate read it as a failed deployment and the rollback undid a perfectly good deploy.
fingerprints.resolution: Distinguish 'the fleet is stopped by design' from 'a bot failed to start': inside the running window the bots must be running (unchanged); outside it the deployment is judged on the restart itself, i.e. trading-bot-manager must be active. The window is read from the VM's clock (bots #357, PR #358). Also note that a deploy failing after 'Record deployed commit on VM' must restore the marker, or the next deploy skips the VM entirely (bots #354, PR #356).

patterns: process is alive but has not sent a heartbeat
fingerprints.symptom: The operator gets a 'CRITICAL TRADING ALERT - Hung Bot Detected: <SYM>' email saying the bot's process is alive but has not sent a heartbeat for N minutes, while the same fault is also reported by the supervisor as a crash loop. The bot is not hung: it is dying at boot and being restarted, so between two restarts a live process exists while the heartbeat stays frozen at the last successful one.
fingerprints.root_cause: The watchdog decides liveness by sampling the pidfile's pid (os.kill(pid, 0) plus a /proc/<pid>/cmdline check), so it observes a crash-looping bot as 'alive' during the instant between two restarts, and a stale Firestore heartbeat then reads as a hang. It samples liveness and never sees deaths, so the supervisor's crash-loop detection (D21, bots #355) does not cover it and the two alerts contradict each other about one fault. The pidfile already carried the discriminator - bot_manager._write_pidfile writes '<pid>\n<start_epoch>' - but only the pid was read.
fingerprints.resolution: Read the start epoch from the pidfile and suppress the hung event while the current process instance is younger than the heartbeat timeout (a process that has just started has not yet had a full window to heartbeat, so a stale heartbeat belongs to a dead predecessor). An unknown or negative uptime still alerts, so a real hang is never silenced. bots #363.

patterns: No recent VM health snapshot is available
The ops-watchdog timer (every 15 min) has not reported within the last hour
fingerprints.symptom: The daily summary digest (16:00 ET) includes a LOW priority alert saying 'No recent VM health snapshot is available. The ops-watchdog timer (every 15 min) has not reported within the last hour -- check ops-watchdog.service/.timer on the VM.'
fingerprints.root_cause: When ops-watchdog.timer was introduced (Issue #310), deploy-services.yml did not enable or start ops-watchdog.timer. It remained disabled/inactive on the VM, so ops-watchdog.sh never ran and system_health/current in Firestore went stale/missing. Additionally, weekday-only timers lacked weekend staleness tolerance in ops-watchdog.sh.
fingerprints.resolution: Enable ops-watchdog.timer with `sudo systemctl enable --now ops-watchdog.timer` in deploy-services.yml. Also add weekend tolerance (+52h on Sat, Sun, Mon) in ops-watchdog.sh for weekday-only timers (trade-log-auditor, learning-analysis).
fingerprints.verification_cmd: gcloud compute ssh trading-bot-vm --zone=us-central1-a --command='systemctl status ops-watchdog.timer'

patterns: TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a real number, not 'NoneType'
Broker Client ID Conflict - Restart Failure Persisting
fingerprints.symptom: Bot crash-loops upon startup or during bar processing with 'TypeError: float() argument must be a string or a real number, not 'NoneType'', prompting the supervisor to issue a persistent failure notification (often misidentified as an IBKR Client ID 326 conflict).
fingerprints.root_cause: When market indicators (e.g. iv, iv_rank, hv, adx, atr) contain explicit None values (e.g. when option quotes return empty/no conId), dict.get('iv', 0.0) returns None because the key is present in the dictionary. Casting this with float() raises TypeError and crashes the bot loop.
fingerprints.resolution: Use safe float coercion helper (_safe_float) across adaptive agents and orchestrators to safely handle None and non-numeric types. Add defensive try-except fallback in options_manager and base.py so secondary overlay failures never terminate core bot execution.

patterns: Position creation timed out waiting for bot response
The bot may be offline or delayed. Please check bot logs and status
Blocking order execution: IBKR unhealthy (Market data stale
IBKR connection unhealthy: Market data stale
fingerprints.symptom: Operator attempts to create position from dashboard; UI times out after 45s with warning 'Position creation timed out waiting for bot response. The bot may be offline or delayed.', while bot log reports 'Blocking order execution: IBKR unhealthy (Market data stale)'.
fingerprints.root_cause: 1) IBKRHealthMonitor hardcoded a 120s staleness threshold which is shorter than the 300s (5-min) bar cadence, falsely blocking execution for 60% of the session. 2) The bot pending command check was tied to the 60s heartbeat while dashboard polling timed out after 45s.
fingerprints.resolution: Scale IBKRHealthMonitor stale data threshold dynamically based on bar_size/stale_data_timeout (450s-600s). Decouple pending command polling to run every 3s in the heartbeat loop. Increase dashboard UI maxAttempts from 30 (45s) to 50 (75s).
